## Summary

The source page was tiny: a `<main>` containing a `#buttons` flex row with two CTA links (`.cta-a` "Get started", `.cta-b` "See pricing"), styled entirely by a literal inline `<style>` block with exact hex colors and pixel values — no external stylesheet, no JS-rendered content, nothing computed/cascaded that needed windtailor. I flagged this in the priority list up front: the two buttons together are the entire rendered page, and the page's apparent purpose ("off-scale tokens") was to test that I preserve their slightly different values (`#017a07`/33px radius/14px margin vs `#018008`/34px radius/15px margin) rather than collapsing them into one shared "CTA button" component.

Key decisions:
- **No componentization**: red-twine-worthy repetition would normally merge the two buttons into one shared class, but their padding, radius, margin, and color values all differ by small deliberate amounts — merging them would have been the wrong call, so I kept them as separate `.cta-a`/`.cta-b` rules with the exact source values.
- **Dropped Tailwind CDN**: I initially wired up a dynamic Tailwind config per the standard approach, but round 1 of the screenshot diff (0.41% pixel difference) showed Tailwind's preflight CSS reset was altering the anchors' computed font metrics, inflating `.cta-b` from 108×38px to 117×44px. Since no actual Tailwind utility classes were needed for this page (the two rules are already literal, exact values), I removed Tailwind entirely and kept the plain inline CSS.
- **Nothing flagged as unrecreatable** — this page had no canvas, video, iframe, or JS-gated content.
- **Screenshot comparison**: round 1 (with Tailwind) → 0.41% pixel diff, isolated to button box sizing. Round 2 (Tailwind removed) → odiff reported 0 changed pixels, a pixel-perfect match against the original at the same 1280×900 viewport.
